title: Per-tenant Commitment: Virtual Credit Buckets and Late Adjustment Billing PRD
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Implement a per-tenant "virtual credit" commitment mechanism to allow customers to pre-allocate committed compute/usage in flexible buckets that roll forward, support late adjustments, and produce clear invoice line items. This PRD defines product requirements, acceptance criteria, API contracts, billing reconciliation, migration paths for existing committed plans, and rollout controls.
background: Enterprise customers have asked for more flexible commitment constructs that let them prepay or reserve capacity across models and routes without rigid per-model purchase commitments. Current 'reserved capacity' and monthly credits are too coarse for teams that want: per-tenant priority routing, the ability to increase and retroactively apply extra credits for prior usage windows, and transparent invoice line items specifying applied virtual credits. We need a feature that minimizes billing disputes and supports late adjustments up to a configurable reconciliation window.
goals: Create virtual credit buckets that map to a tenant and can be scoped to: global, per-environment, or per-route
Support time-windowed commitments (monthly/quarterly) with auto-rollforward or expire behavior
Allow admins to submit late adjustments (increase/decrease commitment) within a reconciliation window (default 30 days) which triggers invoice re-calculation or credit memo workflow
Expose APIs and Console UX for purchasing, assigning, and viewing virtual credit usage and projections
Produce explicit invoice line items and accounting-ready export for reconciliations
non_goals: Replacing existing Dedicated SKU reservations (this will integrate but not deprecate)
Complex per-token micro-pricing negotiation flows (outside of standard per-credit unit price)
Automated tax calculations (will rely on billing platform integrations)
requirements: Create a VirtualCreditBucket object: id, tenant_id, name, scope (global/env/route), units_total, units_remaining, purchase_date, window_start, window_end, rollforward_policy (auto/expire), price_per_unit, refundable_flag
Tenant admin can purchase or top-up a bucket via Console or Billing API
Usage engine must debit buckets in priority order: explicitly assigned bucket -> route-scoped -> env-scoped -> global
Support soft caps with callbacks: when remaining units fall below threshold X% send webhook and Console alert
Late adjustment API: allow admin to increase or decrease units_total within 30-day default reconciliation window; decreases create credit memos; increases can be applied retroactively to close gaps
Invoice generator must emit line items: purchase, applied-usage, adjustment-credit, adjustment-debit, expiration-writeoff
Reporting: per-bucket consumption timeseries, forecast projection using trailing 7/30-day burn rates
Access controls: only billing admins or roles with 'billing.modify' can do late adjustments
Telemetry events: virtual_credit.purchase, virtual_credit.apply, virtual_credit.adjust, virtual_credit.expire, virtual_credit.topup
Migration utility: map existing committed credits and reserved capacity into initial VirtualCreditBucket(s) with mapping rules
api_contract: POST /v1/billing/tenants/{tenant_id}/buckets - body: {name, scope, scope_id?, units, price_per_unit, window_start, window_end, rollforward_policy}
GET /v1/billing/tenants/{tenant_id}/buckets - list buckets with units_remaining and applied_routes
Webhook: virtual_credit.threshold_exceeded - payload includes tenant_id, bucket_id, remaining_pct
console_ux_notes: New Billing > Commitments page lists buckets with visual burn bars and projected exhaustion date
Bucket detail panel shows applied routes, burn chart (7/30/90 day), adjustment history, invoices referencing the bucket
Top-up flow: quick modal to add units with confirmation of invoice impact and proration preview
Late adjustment flow: wizard with required justification and preview of invoice delta; require 2FA for adjustments affecting >$50k
billing_workflow: Purchases create liability line items and a bucket resource. Applied usage consumes units and generates a 'virtual_credit.apply' record tied to the usage event and invoice id. Adjustments inside the reconciliation window cause invoice updates: decreases produce credit memos applied to the most recent invoice(s) in chronological order; increases may be marked as retroactive charge and appended to the next invoice unless customer requests immediate invoice re-bill. Expired units follow rollforward_policy: auto-rollforward merges remaining units into the next window or expiration generates an 'expiration-writeoff' line item. All automatic changes must be represented in exported invoices for accounting.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Create bucket - API creates a bucket and Console shows it with correct scope and initial units; units_remaining == units_total
AC2: Consumption - when tenant sends usage with route tag, system debits appropriate bucket and emits virtual_credit.apply event; units_remaining decrements and matches usage units
AC3: Priority routing - if multiple buckets apply, debit order (route-scoped, env-scoped, global) is enforced and deterministic
AC4: Low-threshold alerting - when units_remaining < 10% for a bucket, webhook and Console alert are triggered within 60s
AC5: Late increase - increasing units_total inside reconciliation window can be applied to past usage: invoicing reflects retroactive application and finance export shows adjustment line item
AC6: Late decrease - decreasing units_total produces an immediate credit memo and invoice delta; finance export contains credit memo and explains reason
AC7: Rollforward - buckets with rollforward_policy=auto merge remaining units into next period and produce a rollforward audit record
AC8: Invoice visibility - all bucket-related line items appear in tenant invoices and CSV export; sample invoice for test tenant contains at least one purchase, one apply, and one adjustment line
AC9: Migration - migration job maps existing reserved credits into buckets and total units conserved; pilot tenant migrated with zero data loss and reconciled invoice
AC10: Access controls - attempts by non-billing-admin to call adjust API returns 403
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: bucket burn rate heatmap, buckets near expiration, top customers by retroactive adjustments. Alerts: SLO breaches on webhook delivery, >5% mismatch between applied units and invoice applied-usage line items for any tenant for 24h.
migration_plan: Phase 0 (pilot): create migration job to transform reserved_capacity records for 3 pilot customers into per-tenant buckets; manual validation of invoices
Phase 1: run migration for 10% of customers who have commitments under $50k; provide a support runbook
Phase 2: open self-serve migration tool for customers to opt-in
Fallback: retain old reserved_capacity records until reconciliation window closes; ability to rollback mappings
rollout_plan: Internal alpha: enable feature flags for platform and billing teams; endpoints only
Beta: enable for selected customers and invite-only Console controls; collect feedback
GA: public on Console and API; backfill migration tool; release billing-2025.03
risks_mitigation: Risk: Retroactive charges create billing disputes - Mitigation: conservative default (do not auto-rebill invoices unless tenant opted-in) and require invoice preview/ack for retro-bills >$5k
Risk: Complexity in reconciliation - Mitigation: create finance export schema and run parallel validation for 2 billing cycles before GA
Risk: Abuse of late adjustments - Mitigation: audit trail + approval threshold + rate limits on adjust API
security_considerations: All adjust endpoints require billing.modify role and 2FA for high-value adjustments. Audit logs retained for 365 days. Adjust API calls write immutable audit records including actor, justification, and IP.
open_questions: Q1: What is the canonical unit for 'units' across models (tokens vs. compute_seconds vs. normalized_credit)? Decision: use normalized_credits with an exchange table maintained by ModelOnboarding team
Q2: Should we allow negative top-ups (i.e., immediate decrease) beyond reconciliation window? Decision pending finance input
Q3: How to handle refunds for expired units when refund policy is enabled? Need legal input
